analysisRule.name: GALAXY-RULE-2 (committed here before the follow-up code existed)
steps: M1 the statistic: at the refined best lag, over the n samples the template covers, chi2_min = sum w_i f_i^2 - S^2 / T (the weighted sum of squares of the high-passed spectrum minus the part the best-fit template amplitude explains, with S, T and w_i as in X3), with nu = n - 2 degrees of freedom (the amplitude and the lag). The result always carries chi2_min, nu and their ratio.

M2 the cut: under an exact template and independent white noise of the stated sigma, chi2_min is chi-square distributed with nu degrees of freedom up to the variance the high-pass removes (a factor of about 1 - 1/101, which makes the test conservative, never too strict). The refusal fires when chi2_min exceeds the 1 - 1e-4 quantile of chi-square with nu degrees of freedom (the statistics kernel's chi2Quantile): a false refusal rate of 1e-4 per spectrum under the model's own assumptions. The level 1e-4 is a design choice of this kernel stated here, not a published value.

M3 when it fires, with the option refuseMisfit true, the answer is status 'refused' with code 'template-misfit', the redshift withheld, and chi2_min, nu and the quantile named; with the option off (the default) the answer is what it was and the statistic is reported beside it with the flag 'misfit' when the cut is crossed.

M4 the statistic is tested only when sigma was supplied: without a sigma the noise level comes from the spectrum's own successive differences, which carry the line power, and the test would measure the scatter against itself; then the result says 'misfit-untested: errors from scatter'. A peak refused for significance or ambiguity is refused before the test.
analysisRule.assumes: the stated per-pixel sigma is right (a wrong sigma is a wrong test); independent noise; the template, if it is the object, equals it up to an amplitude and a shift, so any structure in the spectrum the template does not carry is a misfit by this test, including a line the template lacks and a line-width difference at high signal to noise
